title: Stuck canary state and version pinning: timeline, root cause, and remediation
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: A model rollout entered a stuck canary state due to an interplay between version pinning and the rollback handler; resulting in residual traffic to the canary and degraded throughput for pinned customers. This ticket tracks the timeline, root cause analysis, and concrete action items to prevent recurrence.
impact: Between 2026-03-02 07:40 and 2026-03-02 09:20 UTC ~15% of production requests to the europe-west1 region were routed to a pinned canary variant that had degraded tokenization performance. Observed effects: 5-10% tail latency increase for affected tenants, error rates for long-sequence generation increased from 0.2% to 1.6%. Two enterprise customers reported degraded response times; no data exfiltration or model output integrity issues identified.
timeline:
2026-03-02 07:36 UTC - Automated rollout to model-v2-canary begins
2026-03-02 07:40 UTC - Canary healthcheck shows elevated decode latency (alerts fired to SRE)
2026-03-02 07:48 UTC - Rollout controller observes metric regressions and initiates automated rollback
2026-03-02 07:49 UTC - Rollback API call returns 202 accepted but subsequent routing update fails intermittently due to rate-limited control-plane write (cp-worker-3)
2026-03-02 07:50-08:05 UTC - Partial rollback: control-plane applied routing table update for 80% of nodes; remaining 20% retained pin flag in canary_state table
2026-03-02 08:08 UTC - Autoscaler sees unusual connection patterns and scales pools conservatively, amplifying degraded tail latency
2026-03-02 08:18 UTC - On-call manually forces canary unpin (routing-matrix v2 API) and triggers a cleanup job; traffic returns to expected distribution by 08:22 UTC
2026-03-02 09:00 UTC - Post-incident triage call; decision to open this follow-up ticket for long-term fixes
root_cause: Two contributing defects aligned: 1) The version-pin API writes were not fully idempotent under partial failures: rollback flow assumed the routing-matrix update would be atomic across control-plane shards but control-plane uses eventual convergence and the cp-worker component was rate-limited, leaving stale entries in the canary_state table. 2) The rollout guardrails did not validate global route convergence post-rollback: the canary lived in a half-committed state with pin=true in ~20% of nodes which continued to accept A/B routing binds. The combination allowed residual client sessions and sticky routing to persist to the degraded canary.
detection: Alerts: infra.alerts#latency-tail, rollout.alerts#canary-regression. Customer reports via support noting slow responses. Grafana anomaly detection flagged increased 95th/99th percentile decode time for model-v2-canary. Incident created from paging and support escalation.
mitigation: Immediate mitigations performed: 1) Manual unpin via routing-matrix v2 API and forced sync job (control-plane job cp-20260302-07) to reconcile canary_state across shards. 2) Temporarily increased capacity in europe-west1 to absorb backlog and reduce tail latency. 3) Short-term rollout freeze for model-v2 variants until follow-ups are implemented.
action_items: OWNER: Diego Morales - Implement a post-rollback convergence check that verifies routing-matrix entries across all control-plane shards before marking rollback complete. ETA: 2026-03-18
OWNER: Claire Ng - Add end-to-end test to the rollout pipeline that simulates partial control-plane failures and validates idempotent unpin semantics. ETA: 2026-03-15
OWNER: SRE Team - Add Grafana dashboard panel (rollout.convergence) that shows live shard-level pin counts and a Prometheus metric for 'stale_pin_count'. ETA: 2026-03-12
OWNER: Diego Morales - Rate-limit backoff: make rollback writes use exponential backoff with bounded retries and produce a safety stop if >X% of shards report pending state. ETA: 2026-03-20
OWNER: Product/Platform - Update rollout runbook to include explicit manual unpin steps and verification checklist (who can execute, required logs). ETA: 2026-03-10
OWNER: Security - Verify that canary unpin workflow continues to meet RBAC expectations when executed manually; document audit steps. ETA: 2026-03-22
notes: PM review (Liam O'Rourke): prioritize preflight checks for pin operations in the rollout pipeline.
Design feedback (Nora Blake): consider UX guardrail in Console that surfaces 'stuck canary' state and blocks new rollouts until resolved.
SRE comment: add incident-specific runbook snippet to avoid repeated manual fixes; automate reconcile-job and run as a controlled cron until fixed.
links: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1a2b3c-incident-artifacts - Attachments: support tickets, heap dumps, control-plane logs
follow_up: Primary focus is on making rollback and pin/unpin operations observable and strongly consistent from the caller's perspective. Secondary work items include improving Console UX and adding automated reconciliation that only runs under a safe rate-limited mode. We'll re-check incident metrics after completing the first three action items and close this ticket when the convergence check is merged, end-to-end test added, and dashboard live.
compliance_notes: No customer data exposure detected. Audit logs for pin/unpin operations retained for 90 days per platform retention policy. Manual unpin steps were performed by SRE and recorded in audit trail cp-audit-20260302-9.
